recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-16135; future category-definition changes should use the UTG/THO process, with separate reconciliation only for distinct applied FHIR decisions.
issue_request: The Published/Persuasive with Modification Jira asked to clarify Observation category semantics: categories are high-level groupings, procedure and therapy remain distinct, questionnaire-derived observations belong under survey, social-history should remove administrative demographics and include familial/environmental health-risk language, imaging should say observations regarding imaging modalities, and laboratory should include digital pathology.
initial_application: Commit efab7476097644c09577492e10eaa99988210c61 (GF#16135) changed the then-core source/observation/codesystem-observation-category.xml definitions for social-history, imaging, and laboratory to match the approved resolution. Procedure, therapy, and survey retained existing definitions that were consistent with the implementation choice at that time.
additional_context: The Observation category CodeSystem is no longer authored in the FHIR core checkout. Commit 5c0494aacfd0b8bd52bc72c587aa89d0a64246f8 removed UTG-maintained terminology content from core, including source/observation/codesystem-observation-category.xml. The active current core source keeps Observation.category bound to ValueSet/observation-category, whose compose imports http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/observation-category. Current THO version 2.0.0 carries the FHIR-16135 definitions, and later FHIR-36305/UP-738 work makes the survey/questionnaire wording explicit.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The build-scoped FHIR core ValueSet already points at the authoritative THO CodeSystem, and that CodeSystem contains the required Observation category definitions.
